reason: REFUTED. The fix rests on a claim that driving the master falsifies: 'the rail marker becomes the single statement of today, and it already sits where the reading starts.' The rail marker is the one that does NOT survive reading. At 1280 and 1440 the horizon sits in .b-stick (b.css:1279, position:sticky, comment: 'The horizon does not scroll away'), so .b-todayLabel pins at y=324 and stays in view at EVERY scroll position; .b-origin is position:absolute top:0 inside .b-measure and leaves the viewport after ~400px of scroll. Measured on owner-flight 1440x960: scroll 410 -> origin y=-128 (out of view), label y=324 (in view), 6 dates on screen; scroll 1170 -> origin y=-888, label y=324, 6 dates. Same at 1280x900 and on desk 1440x960. Deleting .b-todayLabel therefore leaves every scrolled desktop view showing six to seven dates with no statement of today anywhere on screen - the paid-for 'Unanchored time' defect reintroduced at the widest and most-used width, in exchange for removing one small mono label. Second, independently fatal: .b-origin carries aria-hidden="true" (render-b.js:179; verified in the DOM), .b-todayLabel does not. The label is the ONLY statement of today in the accessibility tree on owner, phone and desk. Deleting it also breaches the paid-for lesson 'State carried only visually - the same fact must exist in words in the accessible name.' Third, the fix orphans .b-todayRule, the single indigo hairline the CSS names as 'the one thing indigo is spent on at the top of the page' (b.css:95); the proposal deletes its caption and keeps the rule, leaving an uncaptioned accent line. Fourth, 'pass stamp:false on the owner surface' conflates two different facts: 'Live since' is F.publication.publishedAt (when guests got a copy), 'Updated' is F.updatedLabel (when the plan was last edited); they read alike only because the fixture sets publishedAt = UPDATED (fixture.js:118, 182). Suppress the stamp and an owner who edits after publishing is shown a publication date where a revision date belongs. The finding is also overstated on its own measurement: at 1440 the two labels are 402px apart centre to centre (label 186-530, origin 710-809), not 'about 700px', and below 1280 they are in the same single column 105-129px apart, where the duplication reads as an anchor restated at the instrument rather than as two voices. The only residual kernel is on paper, where '79 days away on Thursday 16 July 2026' and 'Today, Thursday 16 July 2026' do state one day twice - but the unit line dates the FIGURE and the origin labels the AXIS, they are two objects, and that narrow point does not carry the delete-everywhere proposal that is the finding.
sharpenedFix: If anything is worth doing here it is print-only and small: in measure(), when o.medium === 'print', render the origin as 'Today' alone, since countBlock() already prints '... away on Thursday 16 July 2026' directly above it. Leave .b-todayLabel untouched at every screen medium - it is the sticky, accessible, indigo-captioned anchor - and leave foot()'s stamp alone on the owner surface, since 'Live since' and 'Updated' are different facts that only coincide in the fixture.
